name: What the Customs House Was Counting

levels.entry: Boards fixed to the wall of the weighing floor, cut with rows of marks. A tally of something.
Two columns. The left is quantities and the right is a rate — this is a tariff, posted where the payer could see it.
The goods are named in a trade shorthand. Grain, oil, salt, and one I cannot read at all, which is charged at nine times the rate of salt.
Tolu. Teshk uses the word for the shallow water at the head of a channel — so the ninefold rate was on something that only came in on a shallow draught.
The last board is unfinished. Ruled, and the first two rows cut, and then nothing — which is not what abandonment looks like. Somebody stopped in the middle of a morning.

notes: The map's clock. An unfinished tariff board dates the ending to a day rather than a century, which is what makes the sudden reading arguable.
